title: Derived scalar realization of sequences of varying coefficient modules
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R,B_n$ for $n\ge1$ be sheaves of commutative rings on it, with maps $q_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ and $\pi_n:R\to B_n$ satisfying $q_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in a universe containing the site and the module categories. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], applied termwise and localized at quasi-isomorphisms, gives functors $S_n:D(B_n)\to D(B_{n+1})$ along $q_n$ and $Q_n:D(B_n)\to D(R)$ along $\pi_n$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$\gamma_n:Q_{n+1}S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n,$$
induced on complexes by the identity on the underlying abelian sheaves: in each degree, for every site object $U$, $r\in R(U)$ acts on both sides through $\pi_n(r)=q_n(\pi_{n+1}(r))$. For $m\ge n$ the analogous comparison for $B_m\to B_n$ is the iterated composite of the $\gamma_i$ with the intervening restrictions; for $m=n$ it is the identity, and these comparisons satisfy composition through every intermediate level.

Let $\mathscr E$ have objects $M=(M_n,d_n)$ with $M_n\in D(B_n)$ and $d_n:M_{n+1}\to S_nM_n$. Its morphisms $a:M\to N=(N_n,e_n)$ are families $a_n:M_n\to N_n$ satisfying $S_n(a_n)d_n=e_na_{n+1}$, with componentwise identities and composition. There is a functor
$$\mathcal U:\mathscr E\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf Z_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},D(R))$$
[def-weil-inverse-system], whose levels are $Q_nM_n$, consecutive transitions are $t_n^M=\gamma_n(M_n)\circ Q_{n+1}(d_n)$, and whose value on $a$ has components $Q_n(a_n)$. These transitions determine every longer transition by composition and the length-zero transition by identity. Explicitly,
$$Q_n(a_n)t_n^M=t_n^NQ_{n+1}(a_{n+1}).$$
If every $a_n$ is invertible, $\mathcal U(a)$ is an isomorphism with inverse components $Q_n(a_n^{-1})$ satisfying
$$t_n^M Q_{n+1}(a_{n+1}^{-1})=Q_n(a_n^{-1})t_n^N.$$
Its two composites are the componentwise identities. Objects and arrows of $\mathscr E$ are specified in the individual derived categories; no simultaneous complex representative, flatness of $q_n$, completeness, or boundedness is required.

proof.text: For each map of ring sheaves in the statement, restriction of scalars is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction]. The site is small in the specified module universe, so its sheafification hypotheses hold. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to each restriction functor: the termwise functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms and factors through the ordinary unbounded derived category. This gives the functors $S_n$ and $Q_n$ with their comparison isomorphisms to termwise restriction after cochain localization. The same applies to restriction along every composite $q_{n,m}=q_n\circ\cdots\circ q_{m-1}:B_m\to B_n$ ($q_{n,n}=1$).

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), with sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian) for exact scalar restriction

proof.text: Write $\rho_f$ for ordinary restriction along a ring-sheaf map $f$. By [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], for a $B_n$-module sheaf $H$, the identity of its underlying abelian sheaf is an isomorphism $\rho_{\pi_{n+1}}\rho_{q_n}H\to\rho_{\pi_n}H$: at $U$, its source action is $r\cdot h=q_n(\pi_{n+1}(r))h=\pi_n(r)h$, the target action. It commutes with restrictions in $U$ and with every module map because those underlying maps are unchanged. Applying these identity maps in every degree gives a natural isomorphism of cochain functors, since the differentials are also unchanged. More generally the same identity construction compares iterated restriction along any finite chain with restriction along its composite. Both ways of composing such comparisons are identities on each underlying group, so agree; the empty chain gives the identity.

source.place: Tag 03CV (definition-sheaf-modules); agent-written sectionwise calculation from the definition of scalar restriction

proof.text: Use the factorization isomorphisms of Step 1 to regard $Q_{n+1}S_n$ and $Q_n$, after precomposition with the localization of $B_n$-complexes, as lifts of the two cochain functors of Step 2 followed by $R$-cochain localization. These cochain functors invert quasi-isomorphisms by Step 1. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] uniquely lifts their identity-on-underlying-sheaves natural isomorphism to $\gamma_n:Q_{n+1}S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n$. Its normalization on localized complexes is precisely the Step 2 identity conjugated by the factorization isomorphisms, as specified by that clause. Apply the same construction to each finite chain to obtain the analogous derived composition comparisons. This constructs natural transformations on all derived arrows, rather than only on maps with a selected cochain representative. In Lean, comparison is the inverse exact-functor compositor followed by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso of the normalized ordinary comparison. The existing mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom_app_factors formulas prove the normalization after cancellation of the compositor.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), with fully faithful precomposition on natural transformations as stated in the cited localization node

proof.text: For a finite chain, compare its direct restriction comparison with the iterated adjacent comparisons, inserting the termwise factorization isomorphisms. On precomposition with the cochain localization the inserted isomorphisms cancel in adjacent pairs, leaving in both cases the identity of the underlying complex from Step 2. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore makes the two derived natural transformations equal. The same calculation for a chain cut at any intermediate index gives the claimed composition law, and for a chain of length zero gives the identity. This verifies coherence in each individual source derived category; it does not select representatives for a sequence of objects or arrows. The Lean proof reuses the already proved localization coherence API in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.MapDerivedCategoryMate: preservation of composition and whiskering by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, associativity of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, and its identity law. Ordinary comparison inverses are identities on sections, so their two composites agree by sectionwise extensionality. These API identities transfer this equality to comparison_assoc. For finite_comparison, the zero case cancels the derived identity comparison; the successor case uses comparison_assoc, naturality of the adjacent comparison, and the induction hypothesis. projection_chain is a separate induction using the compatibility of the coefficient projections.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization); agent-written equality check using the natural-transformation uniqueness in the cited node

proof.text: The displayed objects and arrows of $\mathscr E$ form a category: identity families satisfy the compatibility equation by functoriality of $S_n$, and if $a:M\to N$ and $b:N\to P$ satisfy it, then $S_n(b_na_n)d_n=S_n(b_n)e_na_{n+1}=f_nb_{n+1}a_{n+1}$, where $f_n$ is the transition of $P$. Associativity and units hold componentwise. For $M$, put $T_n=Q_nM_n$ and $t_n=\gamma_n(M_n)Q_{n+1}(d_n)$. Define $T_{m,n}=t_n\cdots t_{m-1}$ for $m>n$ and $T_{n,n}=1$. Associativity gives $T_{m,n}T_{k,m}=T_{k,n}$ for $k\ge m\ge n$, including equality cases. Thus these are inverse systems exactly as defined in [def-weil-inverse-system].

source.place: Tag 0030 (definition-system-over-poset); componentwise category laws and finite composites

proof.text:
For $a:M\to N$, naturality of $\gamma_n$ and then the defining equation of $a$ give
$$Q_n(a_n)\gamma_n(M_n)Q_{n+1}(d_n)=\gamma_n(N_n)Q_{n+1}(S_n(a_n)d_n)=\gamma_n(N_n)Q_{n+1}(e_na_{n+1})=t_n^NQ_{n+1}(a_{n+1}).$$
For a transition of length zero the compatibility is the identity equation. Inductively, compatibility for a composite of $r+1$ consecutive transitions follows by substituting the consecutive equation and then the length-$r$ equation. Hence the components $Q_n(a_n)$ form a morphism of the inverse systems by [def-weil-inverse-system]. Since each $Q_n$ preserves identity and composition, these assignments preserve componentwise identities and composition, and define $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 0030 (definition-system-over-poset); agent-written naturality calculation and induction on transition length

proof.text:
Suppose every $a_n$ is invertible. Starting with the consecutive equation in Step 6, compose on the left with $Q_n(a_n^{-1})$ and on the right with $Q_{n+1}(a_{n+1}^{-1})$. The inverse identities and functoriality give
$$t_n^M Q_{n+1}(a_{n+1}^{-1})=Q_n(a_n^{-1})t_n^N.$$
Thus the proposed inverse components are a morphism of inverse systems by [def-weil-inverse-system] (the longer equations follow by the same induction). Their composites with $\mathcal U(a)$ have components $Q_n(a_n^{-1}a_n)=1$ and $Q_n(a_na_n^{-1})=1$, respectively. They are therefore the identity morphisms of the towers. Steps 5–7 took place entirely in the individual derived categories and used only functoriality, naturality and finite composition. Step 1 required exact scalar restriction, which holds for arbitrary ring-sheaf maps; no flatness, completeness or boundedness enters.
